script.base: JAX is a -8.5 home favorite with a 40.5 total, so the book’s script is Jacksonville 24.5 and Cleveland 16.0, not a shootout. Base flow: JAX leads by halftime and runs the clock late, so the higher-usage JAX back’s carries rise; CLE, down 8.5 with a 16-point team total, falls behind and abandons the run. Pace stays modest.
script.flip1: CLE hangs within one score into the fourth. Both sides stay balanced, Quinshon Judkins keeps a real carry count toward his 60.5 rush median, and JAX cannot just bleed clock, so Chris Rodriguez Jr. rush volume and CLE’s pass-only tilt both come in lighter than the base script.
script.flip2: JAX jumps ahead early and it becomes a blowout (spread already 8.5, so late starter snaps are at risk). CLE’s run dies completely and garbage-time throws go to Harold Fannin Jr., Jerry Jeudy, Isaiah Bond and Dylan Sampson, while the JAX lead back piles early rush yards then may sit. Unsaved outdoor weather could also drag the 40.5 total into a slog.

pre_mortem: Monday both legs lost because the 2025 medians were not 2026 roles. Judkins under died if Cleveland established the run in a 16-point game anyway, Brailsford played, and he hit one 40-plus run like the 91 already in the last4 — the line is his own 14-game median, so a normal day does not clear an edge, and there is no JAX run-defense number saying they stuff him. Rodriguez over died if the hot 52/63/65 sample was another offense, Allen played through the hip, and a Tuten committee held him to the 41-yard miss, or JAX fell behind and threw to Washington (last4 53, 145, 115, 87) and Thomas instead of handing it off. No coverage chart and no price means we also cannot claim the number was soft.
slip_story: One favorite-runs-the-clock story only: JAX 24.5 leads and hands it to Rodriguez; CLE at 16 points never gets a positive run script, so Judkins rush stays under 60.5. Those two win together. Do not add JAX WR overs (Washington 52.5, Thomas 49.5, Strange 45.5, Meyers 44.5), which need Jacksonville to throw, or a total over. A CLE pass-catcher would fit the dog-throws flip of this same script, but Jeudy form (3 of 4 under 26.5) and Fannin form (split vs 41.5) are not clean, and the cap is two legs, no TDs, one market per player.
